outcome: Neurodevelopmental abnormalities (developmental delay, cerebral palsy, speech problems, intellectual disability, hyperactivity)
cohort: The study included all live inborn extremely low birthweight (ELBW) infants admitted to the neonatal unit of King Abdulaziz Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between January 1st, 2005 and December 31st, 2007 (n = 117).
finding: More than one-third of ELBW infants died before discharge, and among survivors, two-thirds had one or more neurodevelopmental and/or cognitive abnormalities within their first 6 years of life, with 50% limits of viability identified at 25 weeks' gestation or a birthweight over 600g.
birth_weight: Extremely low birthweight (ELBW) infants, with 50% viability defined as >600g
gest_age: Preterm neonates, with 50% viability defined as 25 weeks' gestation
